children.translated_text: Accompanied by its auto-commentary: Arising, abiding, destruction, existence, non-existence, inferior, equal, and superior—
these were spoken by the <s>Buddha</s> from worldly convention, not from ultimate [truth]. //1//
There is no self, nor indeed non-self, neither self-and-non-self, nor anything other;
all [things] are to be declared empty of <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature), like <s>nirvāṇa</s>. //2//
In the complete assemblage of causes and conditions, or taken separately,
the <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) of all things does not exist; therefore, the empty indeed is found. //3//
An entity does not arise from entities; nor does a non-entity [arise] from non-existence;
not from both existence and non-existence, due to contradiction; nor [are there] abiding and destruction, since there is no arising. //4//

children.text: na jāyate yadā jātaṃ nājātamapi jāyate /
children.translated_text: That which is already born does not arise; that which is unborn also does not arise;
from both the born and the unborn, thus even that which is being born does not arise. //5//

children.text: phale syāt phalavān hetuḥ nāstitve 'hetunā samaḥ /
children.translated_text: A cause that has a fruit would be one possessing fruit; if [the fruit] is non-existent, [the cause] is like a non-cause;
in [the simultaneity of] existence and non-existence there is contradiction; [arising] in the three times is not tenable. //6//
In oneness, multiple occurrences are not [possible]; and in multiplicity, oneness is not [possible];
those things that are dependently originated are without [independent] marks. //7//
The twelve limbs are indeed non-arising; [their] arising is dependently produced;

children.text: ekacitte na tad yuktaṃ bahuṣvapi na yujyate // 8 //
children.translated_text: in a single mind that is not tenable; in many [minds] also it is not tenable. //8//

children.text: ātmā nāsti na cānātmā nityānitye duḥkhaṃ sukham /
children.translated_text: There is no self and no non-self; neither permanent nor impermanent; neither suffering nor happiness;
neither pure nor impure—therefore, the <s>viparyāsas</s> (inversions) do not exist. //9//
In their absence, <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), born of the four inversions, does not [exist];

children.text: tadabhāvānna saṃskārāḥ syuḥ śeṣā api tādṛśāḥ // 10 //
children.translated_text: in its absence, <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) would not exist; the rest are likewise. //10//
When <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) do not exist, there is no <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance); and it does not exist because of the absence of those;
being mutual causes, they are not established by <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature). //11//
What is not established by its own <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature), how could it produce another?
Therefore, those others, not established by others, would not be produced by such conditions. //12//

children.text: pitā putro na putro 'pi pitānyonyaṃ na tau vinā /
children.translated_text: A father is not a son, nor is a son a father; they do not exist without each other;

children.text: tathā na yugapattau hi dvādaśāṅgaṃ tathaiva ca // 13 //
children.translated_text: nor are they simultaneous—the twelve limbs are likewise. //13//

children.text: pratītya viṣayān svapne na syād duḥkhaṃ sukhaṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: Just as in a dream, depending on objects, suffering and happiness would not exist,

children.text: viṣayo na tathaivāpi taṃ pratītya pratītyajaḥ // 14 //
children.translated_text: so too the object is not [ultimately real], and what depends on it, being dependently arisen, [is also not real]. //14//
If things by their nature are not superior, inferior, or middling,
in the absence of diversity, production from causes is not established. //15//

children.text: bhāvāḥ svabhāvataḥ siddhā no 'pratītya pratītya sat /
children.translated_text: Things established by <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) [should exist] without depending [on anything]; what depends [on conditions] exists,
[but] without <s>svabhāva</s>, whence are there things? <s>Svabhāva</s> too is not established. //16//
Where is destruction from <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature), <s>parabhāva</s> (other-nature), or even from non-existence?
<s>Svabhāva</s>, <s>parabhāva</s>, and non-existence—these are <s>viparyāsas</s> (inversions). //17//

children.text: śūnyatve sati notpādo nirodho 'pi na vidyate /
children.translated_text: In emptiness, arising does not exist; cessation also does not exist;
for in the emptiness of <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature), whence would there be arising and passing away? //18//

children.text: abhāve 'sati bhāvo na bhāvābhāvau na caikadā /
children.translated_text: Without non-existence existing, there is no existence; existence and non-existence do not [occur] simultaneously;

children.text: ṛte bhāvaṃ na cābhāvo bhāvo 'bhāvaḥ sadā bhavet // 19 //
children.translated_text: without existence, there is no non-existence; existence would always be non-existence. //19//

children.text: na svato nāpi parato 'bhāvo bhāvaṃ vinā na hi /
children.translated_text: Non-existence [does not arise] from itself, nor from another; non-existence does not [exist] without existence;

children.text: ata eva na bhāvo 'styabhāvo na tadabhāvataḥ // 20 //
children.translated_text: therefore, existence does not exist; non-existence does not [exist] because of the absence of that. //20//
If existence exists, [there is] eternalism; annihilationism from the absence of that;

children.text: ubhayaṃ hi sato bhāvād bhāvo 'to nābhyupeyate // 21 //
children.translated_text: both [follow] from the existence of an entity; therefore, existence is not to be accepted. //21//
From a continuum, not [from a permanent] continuum; an entity perishes having produced [its effect];
this is established not from a [permanent] continuum, and the fault of annihilationism [is refuted] as before. //22//
Having seen [this], the declaration of the path of cessation [was made]; because of emptiness, arising and passing away do not [exist];
moreover, because of mutual contradiction, and because of seeing contradictory things. //23//
If there is no arising and cessation, what <s>nirvāṇa</s> [comes] from cessation?
Is not <s>nirvāṇa</s> the non-arising and non-cessation that exist by <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature)? //24//
If cessation is <s>nirvāṇa</s>, [that would be] annihilationism; eternalism otherwise;
therefore, [<s>nirvāṇa</s>] is neither existence nor non-existence; it is non-arising and non-cessation. //25//
If there is some abiding, that would be <s>nirvāṇa</s>; it could also be non-existence;
but even in non-existence, that [<s>nirvāṇa</s>] is not [found]; even in the absence of non-existence, that too is not [found]. //26//

children.text: na svato lakṣaṇaṃ lakṣyāllakṣyaṃ sidhyati lakṣaṇāt /
children.translated_text: The mark does not establish itself from itself or from the marked; the marked is not established from the mark;
nor [are they established] from each other; for what is unestablished cannot be the establisher of the unestablished. //27//
By this [reasoning], cause and effect, feeling and the one who feels, and so forth,
the seen and the seer and so forth—all, without remainder, have been stated. //28//
Due to the non-establishment of mutual proof, and the non-establishment from itself, and the dissolution,
existence, non-existence, and the three times are mere non-being, conceptual construction. //29//
Arising, duration, and cessation — the threefold characteristic of the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) —
therefore, nothing conditioned exists, nor does the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>). // 30 //

children.text: bhagno na bhajyate 'bhagno 'pyasthitasya na ca sthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: What is destroyed is not being destroyed, and what is not destroyed [has no destruction]; what has not endured has no duration,
and what has endured also has no duration; what has not arisen does not arise. // 31 //
Neither existent, nor non-existent, nor both existent and non-existent, neither one nor many —
all conditioned and unconditioned things have gone into these very categories. // 32 //
There is indeed ownership of <s>karma</s> (action), and there is <s>karma</s> and the fruit of <s>karma</s>;
the Blessed One, the Teacher, taught the non-destruction of <s>karma</s> as well. // 33 //
<s>Karma</s> (action) is said to be unceased, unarisen, and without <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature);
it arises from the grasping of a self, and its producer too is from conceptual construction. // 34 //

children.text: yadi svabhāvataḥ karma tajjaḥ kāyo 'pi śāśvataḥ /
children.translated_text: If <s>karma</s> (action) existed by <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature), the body born from it would also be eternal;
it would not be the ripening of suffering, and the self itself would be <s>karma</s>. // 35 //
<s>Karma</s> (action) is born from conditions, and there is nothing not born from conditions;
all <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) are like an illusion, like a city of <s>gandharvas</s> (celestial beings), like a mirage. // 36 //
<s>Karma</s> (action) has <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) as its cause; <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) arise from afflictions and <s>karma</s>;
and the body too has <s>karma</s> as its cause — all three are empty of <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature). // 37 //

children.text: karmaṇyasati kartā na dvayābhāve na tatphalam /
children.translated_text: When <s>karma</s> (action) does not exist, there is no agent; when both are absent, there is no fruit of that;
when that is absent, there is no experiencer; and because of non-existence, there is isolation. // 38 //
One who saw the emptiness of <s>karma</s> (action) through right knowledge — [for such a one] <s>karma</s> does not [arise];

children.text: karmaṇyasati karmabhyaḥ samutpannā na santi vai // 39 //
children.translated_text: when <s>karma</s> does not exist, those born from <s>karma</s> do not exist indeed. // 39 //
Just as the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, creates [a form] through supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>),
and by that created form yet another is created again, // 40 //
the creation of the <s>Buddha</s> is empty — what then can be said of the creation of that creation?
Whatever existence is merely conceptual construction, so it is for both. // 41 //
The agent is like a magical creation, and <s>karma</s> (action) is similar to the created;
that which exists is empty of <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) — it is merely conceptual construction. // 42 //

children.text: karmakartā na nirvāṇaṃ yadi karma svabhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: If <s>karma</s> (action) existed by <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature), the agent and <s>karma</s> would not [attain] <s>nirvāṇa</s>;

children.text: iṣṭāniṣṭaphalaṃ na syāttadbhāvo yadi nāsti vai // 43 //
children.translated_text: and if that nature does not exist, there would be no pleasant or unpleasant fruit. // 43 //
It exists as 'existent,' it also exists as 'non-existent,' and it exists as 'both existent and non-existent' —
the intentional teachings of the <s>Buddhas</s> are indeed not easy [to understand]. // 44 //

children.text: rūpaṃ ced bhūtato jātaṃ tadrūpaṃ syādatattvataḥ /
children.translated_text: If form (<s>rūpa</s>) were born from the elements (<s>bhūtas</s>), that form would be of non-real nature;
it does not arise from its own nature, nor from another, due to the absence of that. // 45 //
The fourfold essence does not reside in one, nor does a single one reside in the four;
the four great elements being non-existent, how is form (<s>rūpa</s>) dependent [on them] established? // 46 //
It is not a mark because of a mark, for it is not ultimately grasped;

children.text: hetupratyayajaṃ sattve na liṅgaṃ neti yujyate // 47 //
children.translated_text: when existence arises from causes and conditions, it is not proper [to say] that a mark does not exist. // 47 //
If there were a grasping of form (<s>rūpa</s>), it would be a grasping of its own nature;
how can there be a grasping of a non-existent form through a cognition that has a non-existent basis? // 48 //

children.text: buddhyā kṣaṇikayā rūpaṃ nāpyate kṣaṇikaṃ yadā /
children.translated_text: By a momentary cognition, momentary form (<s>rūpa</s>) is not apprehended;
then how is future form or past form grasped? // 49 //

children.text: kadāpi varṇasaṃsthāne yadā naiva pṛthak pṛthak /
children.translated_text: When color and shape are never [grasped] separately from each other,

children.text: naikagraho hi bhinnānāṃ hyubhe rūpaṃ prasidhyataḥ // 50 //
children.translated_text: there is no single grasping of what is distinct, yet both are established as form (<s>rūpa</s>). // 50 //

children.text: na rūpe nāpi madhye hi cakṣurbuddhirna cakṣuṣoḥ /
children.translated_text: The visual cognition is neither in form (<s>rūpa</s>), nor in the middle, nor in the eye, nor between the two;

children.text: cakṣuḥ pratītya rūpaṃ ca viparyāso vikalpanā // 51 //
children.translated_text: dependent on the eye and form — [such cognition] is distortion and conceptual construction. // 51 //

children.text: cakṣuḥ paśyati nātmānaṃ rūpaṃ paśyennu tatkatham /
children.translated_text: The eye does not see itself — how then could it see form (<s>rūpa</s>)?
The eye is without self, and form likewise — so too the remaining <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases). // 52 //
The eye is empty of <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature), and empty of other-nature;
likewise form (<s>rūpa</s>) is empty, and so too the remaining <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases). // 53 //
When one [sense-base] is simultaneous with contact, the others are empty;
the empty does not depend on the non-empty, nor does the non-empty depend on emptiness. // 54 //
There is no conjunction of things with <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature); the triad, though abiding, is also non-existent;
there is no contact with the nature of that self-nature — therefore <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) too has no [real] existence. // 55 //
Consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), having reached either the internal <s>āyatana</s> (sense-base) or the external one,
arises — therefore consciousness is empty, like an illusion, like a mirage. // 56 //
Since consciousness arises in dependence on the knowable, consciousness does not exist as a permanent entity;
and the knower too is non-existent, because of the non-existence of knowledge and the knowable. // 57 //

children.text: kaścinnityo hyanityo vānityaṃ sarvaṃ ca nāsti vā /
children.translated_text: Is anything eternal or non-eternal? And is everything non-eternal or not?

children.text: bhāve nityaṃ hyanityaṃ vā kathaṅkāraṃ tathā bhavet // 58 //
children.translated_text: How could there be the eternal or the non-eternal in [real] existence? // 58 //
Passion (<s>rāga</s>), aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), and delusion (<s>moha</s>) arise from the pleasant, unpleasant, and their distortion —

children.text: pratyayajā hyato rāgo dveṣo mohaśca na svataḥ // 59 //
children.translated_text: For <s>rāga</s> (passion), <s>dveṣa</s> (hatred), and <s>moha</s> (delusion) arise from conditions, therefore not from themselves. (verse 59)
In whom <s>rāga</s> (passion) arises, in that [person] <s>dveṣa</s> (hatred) and <s>moha</s> (delusion) [also arise] from the same [source];

children.text: vikalpato hi jāyante no vikalpo 'pi tattvataḥ // 60 //
children.translated_text: For they arise from conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>); but conceptual construction itself is not real. (verse 60)

children.text: ye vikalpyā na te santi kalpyābhāve kva kalpanam /
children.translated_text: Those that are conceptualized do not exist; in the absence of the conceptualized, where is the conceptualizing?
For since they are produced by conditions, both the conceptualized and the conceptualizing are empty. (verse 61)
Ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), born from the four errors (<s>viparyaya</s>), does not [arise] from seeing reality;

children.text: tadabhāve na saṃskārāḥ syuḥ śeṣā api tādṛśāḥ // 62 //
children.translated_text: In its absence, <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) would not exist; the remaining [links] are likewise. (verse 62)
Whatever arises dependent on whatever, in the absence of that, it does not arise from that;
Both existence and non-existence, both formations and non-formations, are peaceful and quiescent. (verse 63)

children.text: hetupratyayajā bhāvāḥ kalpyante ye ca tatvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Things that arise from causes and conditions and are conceptualized as real—

children.text: proktā śāstrā hyavidyā sā dvādaśāṅgaṃ tato bhavet // 64 //
children.translated_text: That is declared by the Teacher to be <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance); from that the twelve limbs [of dependent origination] arise. (verse 64)
From the correct knowledge that things are empty in nature, <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) [ceases]; from seeing reality,
That indeed is the cessation of ignorance; thereby the twelve limbs cease. (verse 65)
Like <s>māyā</s> (illusion), a mirage, a city of <s>gandharvas</s>, a bubble, and foam,
<s>Saṃskāras</s> (formations) resemble a dream; they appear like a firebrand circle. (verse 66)
No thing whatsoever exists by its own nature (<s>svabhāva</s>); here non-existence too is not found.
Things born from causes and conditions, and non-existence as well — are empty. (verse 67)
Because the own-nature of all things is empty, [the Buddha] has taught
That all things arise dependently — thus the <s>Tathāgata</s> is incomparable. (verse 68)

children.text: tanmātraḥ paramārtho hi bhagavān buddha uktavān /
children.translated_text: For the Blessed <s>Buddha</s> has declared that alone to be the <s>paramārtha</s> (ultimate truth).
Relying on worldly convention (<s>lokavartana</s>), all things are diverse according to their nature. (verse 69)
There is no breaking of worldly discourse; no <s>dharma</s> exists in ultimate reality.
The ignorant person is afraid of the removal of conceptual construction in the Buddhist teaching. (verse 70)
'Dependent on this, this exists' — there is no obstruction to the way of the world.

children.text: pratītyajaḥ sa niḥsattvaḥ santyete niścayaḥ katham // 71 //
children.translated_text: What arises dependently is without self-nature; how then can one be certain 'these exist'? (verse 71)

children.text: tattvānvīkṣārataḥ śrāddha ukte kutrāpi na sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The faithful one, devoted to the investigation of reality, is not fixed in any stated position;
Having attained the method through reasoning, he is peaceful through the abandonment of both existence and non-existence. (verse 72)
Through the knowledge of dependent conditionality, having gone beyond the net of views,
One attains untouched <s>nirvāṇa</s>, having destroyed <s>rāga</s> (passion), <s>pratigha</s> (aversion), and <s>moha</s> (delusion). (verse 73)

body.translated_text: The commentary (<s>vṛtti</s>) on the <s>Śūnyatāsaptati</s> (Seventy Verses on Emptiness), composed by the venerable master <s>Nāgārjuna</s>, is completed.
